Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms are defined as:

1. District is Muara Enim District. 2. District Government is Muara Enim District. 3. Regent is the Regent of Muara Enim. 4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the Muara Enim District Government. 5. Women's Empowerment is the strengthening of human rights, enhancement of Protection efforts, quality of life, and increased participation of women in development. (4)

6. Women's Protection is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear of or have occurred violence against women; 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a Child still in the womb and is not married. 8. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 9. Violence is any act that results in suffering or hardship whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Children's Forum is a vehicle for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 11. Child-Friendly District hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a District that has a development system based on Children's rights through the integration of government commitment and resources, community and business world that is planned in a comprehensive and sustainable manner in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 12. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. (5)

13. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions that result in suffering or hardship physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public realm or in private life. 15. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by means of the threat of Violence, use of Violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefit, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 17. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 18. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 19. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children in a gender-sensitive manner. (6)

21. Repatriation is the effort to return women and Children victims of Violence from abroad to the point of debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Social reintegration is the effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Transit house is a vehicle for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so they can grow and develop properly. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify power relationship gaps between women and men within the family and within the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. (7)

29.

Article 82

The family in efforts to protect women's rights plays a role in:

a. protecting women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades women's dignity; b. providing equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. preventing violations of women's rights in the household.

(18) Paragraph 5

Victim Assistance, Enforcement and Legal Aid Article 21

( 1) Victim assistance, enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 13 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in handling cases of acts of violence against women, especially to provide sanctions against perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/ or victims.

(2) Victim assistance, enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

Article 16

(1) Health rehabilitation as referred to in Article 13 letter b is an effort that includes aspects of:

a. promotive;
b. preventive;
C. curative; and
d. rehabilitative.
(2) Health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours, with quality and in accordance with health service standards.

(15)

(3) Women and children victims of acts of violence and children in conflict with the law have the right to health services free of charge, including:

a. medical services;
b. medicolegal services;
c. psychosocial counseling; and
d. visum.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementing health services as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 71

Special protection for children victims of physical and/or psychological violence as referred to in Article 60 paragraph (1) letter i is carried out through efforts to:

(36)

a. disseminate and socialize the provisions of Laws and Regulations that protect children victims of acts of violence; and

b. monitoring, reporting, and imposing sanctions.

Article 19

(1) The Regency Government may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of violence.

(17)

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) Criteria for women victims of acts of violence who require safe houses include:

a. threatened with life;
b. rejected by family or community; c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/ or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house. (5) The provision of safe house services shall be carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/ volunteers;
b. security officers; and/ or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 15

( 1) Reports of acts of violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of:

a. victims;
b. family;
c. community; and/ or
d. community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may file complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/ or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency responsible for the Protection of Women and Children, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 13, are also authorized to provide assistance in handling victims of acts of violence against women obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 24

(1) Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(2) Social reintegration is aimed so that:

a. women victims of acts of violence can continue their social life again; and
b. women victims of acts of violence can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

Article 22

(1) Victim assistance, enforcement and legal aid services are aimed at providing assistance and protection to women victims of acts of violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and legal certainty.

(2) Types of legal aid services include:

a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of official examination reports;
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal aid in the examination process at court; d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until a final legal decision is reached; and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
(3) The Regional Government shall provide legal aid to women victims of acts of violence based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3), the Regional Government may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/ or other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.

Article 42

( 1) The Regency Government shall provide comprehensive health services for children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the womb.

(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

(25)

a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;

b. exemption from cost burden for malnourished Children, children with disabilities, children with special needs, children infected with HIV/ AIDS, child workers, children victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse, children who are victims of violence, and children victims of human trafficking; and

(3) The Regency Government, community, family and parents shall endeavor that children who are born avoid diseases that threaten survival and/ or cause disability.

Part Two

Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women

Article 23

(1) Repatriation is aimed at returning women victims of acts of violence to their region of origin.

(2) Repatriation of women victims of acts of violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

CHAPTER III

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 25

The Regency Government implements repatriation and social reintegration of women victims of acts of violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

(32) Article 59

Service efforts carried out by the Regency Government for child victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 36 through Article 58 apply mutatis mutandis to service efforts for child victims of acts of violence.

(1) Every child has the right to obtain education and teaching in order to develop their personality and intelligence level in accordance with their interests and talents.

SPECIAL PROTECTION OF CHILDREN

(32) Article 59

Service efforts carried out by the Regency Government for child victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 36 through Article 58 apply mutatis mutandis to service efforts for child victims of acts of violence.

Article 24

(1) Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(2) Social reintegration is aimed so that:

a. women victims of acts of violence can continue their social life again; and

(24) Article 39

(1) Every organizer of educational units must provide opportunities for children to obtain educational services without discrimination.

(2) Every organizer of educational units is prohibited from expelling children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the child's education.

(3) In the event that child victims of acts of Violence experience dropping out of school, organizers of educational units must coordinate with relevant agencies.

Article 42

( 1) The Regency Government shall provide comprehensive health services for children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the womb.

(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

(25)

a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;

b. exemption from cost burden for malnourished Children, children with disabilities, children with special needs, children infected with HIV/ AIDS, child workers, children victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse, children who are victims of violence, and children victims of human trafficking; and

(3) The Regency Government, community, family and parents shall endeavor that children who are born avoid diseases that threaten survival and/ or cause disability.

Article 68

(1) Every Person is obliged to protect children from the influence of pornography and prevent children's access to information containing pornographic elements.

(2) Special Protection for children who are victims of pornography as referred to in Article 60 paragraph (1) letter f is implemented through guidance, accompaniment, and social, physical and mental health recovery efforts.

(3) Guidance, accompaniment, and social, physical and mental health recovery as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 19

(1) The Regency Government may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of violence.

(17)

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) Criteria for women victims of acts of violence who require safe houses include:

a. threatened with life;
b. rejected by family or community; c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/ or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house. (5) The provision of safe house services shall be carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/ volunteers;
b. security officers; and/ or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 52

( 1) Facilitation of the juvenile justice system includes criminal and civil justice.

(2) Facilitation of the criminal justice system as referred to in paragraph ( 1) includes :

a. provision of companions or Child volunteers during examination by investigators;
b. provision of legal aid and psychologist services; c. involving members/investigators of the local police in efforts to prevent the occurrence of criminal acts committed by children or children as victims;

(29)

d. realizing restorative justice processes for children in conflict with the law; and

e. rehabilitation and social reintegration services.

(3) Fulfillment of children's rights in the civil justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) includes provision and delivery of consultation and legal aid services during the judicial process.

(4) In facilitating the juvenile justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), the authorized regional apparatus is the regional apparatus in charge of Women and Child Protection and the Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment has the obligation to accompany child victims and perpetrators, in police examinations, prosecution and in court.

Article 15

( 1) Reports of acts of violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of:

a. victims;
b. family;
c. community; and/ or
d. community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may file complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/ or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency responsible for the Protection of Women and Children, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 13, are also authorized to provide assistance in handling victims of acts of violence against women obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 20

(1) Spiritual guidance as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (2) letter d aims for psychological recovery.

(2) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented based on the principles of:

a. not imposing any religion or belief; and b. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim (self determination).
(3) Spiritual guidance shall be carried out by spiritual guidance officers. (4) Spiritual guidance officers as referred to in paragraph (3) consist of consultants of the Marriage Counseling, Development and Preservation Board, Officers of the Religious Affairs Office, Ustads/Ulama, Pastors, Ministers and other religious leaders who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness.

(37) Article 75

Special Protection for child victims of maltreatment and neglect as referred to in Article 60 paragraph (1) letter m shall be carried out through efforts of supervision, prevention, care, counseling, social rehabilitation, and social assistance.

Article 22

Victim Assistance, Enforcement and Legal Aid Article 21

( 1) Victim assistance, enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 13 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in handling cases of acts of violence against women, especially to provide sanctions against perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/ or victims.

(2) Victim assistance, enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

Part Two

Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women

Article 15

( 1) Reports of acts of violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of:

a. victims;
b. family;
c. community; and/ or
d. community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may file complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/ or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency responsible for the Protection of Women and Children, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 13, are also authorized to provide assistance in handling victims of acts of violence against women obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 16

(1) Health rehabilitation as referred to in Article 13 letter b is an effort that includes aspects of:

a. promotive;
b. preventive;
C. curative; and
d. rehabilitative.
(2) Health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours, with quality and in accordance with health service standards.

(15)

(3) Women and children victims of acts of violence and children in conflict with the law have the right to health services free of charge, including:

a. medical services;
b. medicolegal services;
c. psychosocial counseling; and
d. visum.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementing health services as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 22

(1) Victim assistance, enforcement and legal aid services are aimed at providing assistance and protection to women victims of acts of violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and legal certainty.

(2) Types of legal aid services include:

a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of official examination reports;
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal aid in the examination process at court; d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until a final legal decision is reached; and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
(3) The Regional Government shall provide legal aid to women victims of acts of violence based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3), the Regional Government may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/ or other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.

CHAPTER III

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 24

(1) Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(2) Social reintegration is aimed so that:

a. women victims of acts of violence can continue their social life again; and
b. women victims of acts of violence can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

Article 19

(1) The Regency Government may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of violence.

(17)

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) Criteria for women victims of acts of violence who require safe houses include:

a. threatened with life;
b. rejected by family or community; c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/ or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house. (5) The provision of safe house services shall be carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/ volunteers;
b. security officers; and/ or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VII

SPECIAL PROTECTION OF CHILDREN

Article 52

( 1) Facilitation of the juvenile justice system includes criminal and civil justice.

(2) Facilitation of the criminal justice system as referred to in paragraph ( 1) includes :

a. provision of companions or Child volunteers during examination by investigators;
b. provision of legal aid and psychologist services; c. involving members/investigators of the local police in efforts to prevent the occurrence of criminal acts committed by children or children as victims;

(29)

d. realizing restorative justice processes for children in conflict with the law; and

e. rehabilitation and social reintegration services.

(3) Fulfillment of children's rights in the civil justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) includes provision and delivery of consultation and legal aid services during the judicial process.

(4) In facilitating the juvenile justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), the authorized regional apparatus is the regional apparatus in charge of Women and Child Protection and the Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment has the obligation to accompany child victims and perpetrators, in police examinations, prosecution and in court.

Article 80

(1) The role of the community in efforts to protect women and children:

a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. supervise the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
(2) The role of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) is based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms are defined as:

6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a Child still in the womb and is not married. 8. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 9. Violence is any act that results in suffering or hardship whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Children's Forum is a vehicle for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 11. Child-Friendly District hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a District that has a development system based on Children's rights through the integration of government commitment and resources, community and business world that is planned in a comprehensive and sustainable manner in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 12. (5)

13. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 14. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by means of the threat of Violence, use of Violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefit, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 17. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 20. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children in a gender-sensitive manner. (6)

21. Repatriation is the effort to return women and Children victims of Violence from abroad to the point of debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 22. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 24. Transit house is a vehicle for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so they can grow and develop properly. 25. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the Region. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify power relationship gaps between women and men within the family and within the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. c. preventing violations of women's rights in the household.
